subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Inside Jobs: Employees Who Steal Data
description: A quick win: understand Inside Jobs: Employees Who Steal Data.

hook.text: A hospital receptionist copies patient records and sells them online. Nobody suspects an insider.

buildup.text: Employees at banks, hospitals, and government agencies have direct access to sensitive data.

discovery.text: Insider theft accounts for a significant share of data breaches but gets far less attention.

twist.text: Many insiders are never caught because audit systems trust employees by default.

climax.text: The biggest risk to your data may not be a hacker — it's the person processing your paperwork.

punchline.text: Not every threat comes from outside the building.

quiz.question: Why are insider data thieves hard to catch?
options: Audit systems tend to trust employees by default
